blocks.text: PROFESSOR OWEN ARTHURS (recalled) (via video link)
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
Good morning, Professor Arthurs. Can you hear me clearly?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can, thank you.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you very much. Just for the sake of the recording, would you identify yourself again, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I'm Professor Owen Arthurs from Great Ormond Street Hospital in London.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you very much, professor. We have but one child to ask you about today and he is [Baby Q].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I believe you wrote two separate reports or statements relating to his case; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. Was the first and in effect the substantive report dated 21 January 2020?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Did you subsequently sign a second statement, simply confirming the fact that you had been sent additional material and that that material had not changed your view on the case?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. If I can deal first, therefore, with the material that you received in [Baby Q]'s case. I'm looking at the updated list that is in effect appended to the second of the statements that you made. Did that consist of [Baby Q]'s medical records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: The radiographs, which we will deal with individually in a moment?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Then the statement of Dr Bohin, dated 16 April 2019; the three statements of Dr Evans, dated 21 November 2017, 3 June 2018 and 25 January 2019; and a statement made by Professor Stavros Stivaros, who of course is the neuroradiologist, dated 26 October 2020?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. Can we start, please, with paragraph 4 of your report, dated 21 January 2020. Did you receive, amongst all that other material, ten individual radiographs taken of [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: The first was an abdominal image taken at 07.49 on the morning of 22 June?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Just to put that into context for the jury, [Baby Q] had been born earlier that morning at 04.09, so this is a radiograph taken about 3 hours and 40 minutes after his birth.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Were there then three chest X-rays or radiographs taken, the first on 22 June at 12.39, the second on 25 June at 11.52, and the third later that same day, 25 June, at 20.25?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Just to put those into a chronological framework, the second and third of those, in other words the two taken on 25 June, they are tiles 135 and 217 respectively, and the event, the collapse of [Baby Q], had occurred at 09.10 hours that same morning. So putting that into sequence then, we have [Baby Q]'s collapse -- this is all on 25 June -- at 09.10, tile 101. The first radiograph after the collapse at 11.52, tile 135. And the second after the collapse at 20.25, tile 217.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Moving on then, was the fifth radiograph in the sequence an abdominal image taken the following morning, 26 June, at 05.05 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Just so that we know a bit about what you're about to tell us, that is the one that you identified as showing an abnormality; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So again, just to put that into the chronological context, that image was taken about 20 hours after the event which the prosecution have identified as being relevant in this trial.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then the final five images. Was the first taken the same day as the fifth, so this is the sixth in the total list, 26 June at 11.58?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Followed by two images on 29 June at 07.41 and 08.55?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And a single image of the chest on 30 June at 11.25 and then a lower leg radiograph taken several days later on 3 July?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So taking those five images together, does it come to this, that none of those show any abnormalities and in effect you make no further reference to them in your report?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. Moving on to the medical history, which you set out in your report, did you record the fact that [Baby Q] was born at 31 weeks' gestation on 22 June?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That he was admitted into the neonatal unit, requiring some respiratory support?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Your understanding was that he had appeared well until he suddenly deteriorated --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: -- at the time we have identified? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So moving then, please, to the body of your evidence, which is your review of the imaging. Did you conclude that the two -- the first two images in the list, those taken on 22 June, that they showed no abnormality?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Moving then to images 3, 4 and 5, we have the two taken on the 25th in the aftermath of his collapse, which are tiles 135 and 217. I'm just going to remind the jury of what they looked like, Professor Arthurs, because it's been a while since we have heard this evidence. If Mr Murphy would help us with quickly showing us tile 135.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is 2 hours and 40 minutes after the collapse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is there anything unusual about that image, professor?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. We can comment on the placement of the lines but I don't think they're relevant to the material that's being discussed in this case.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. Moving then to tile 217, please. This is the image of 20.25 on 25 June. Do the same comments apply to that one?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's right. By this stage [Baby Q]'s been intubated and is being ventilated, but there's nothing else really to see on this radiograph.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. So moving, please, to the fifth in the sequence, which is the radiograph taken on 26 June at 05.05 hours. This was in the case papers at page J24266, and you annotated this next image in your report, didn't you, professor?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Do we now see on the screen an image of your annotations?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: If you could take us through this slowly, please. What can you see and explain to us that may be viewed as being abnormal?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. The top of the radiograph, where the writing "26 June 05.05" is, is effectively the diaphragm. So this is an image from below the diaphragm, so the abdomen. The arrows, the white and black arrows, show a single dilated loop of bowel, which is slightly abnormal in this context, and then the circle on your left-hand side shows another area where there could be abnormalities within the bowel called pneumatosis.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Let's deal with what we can see in the circle then first of all. Pneumatosis, what does that mean in language that I'll be able to understand, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Pneumatosis is where gas within the bowel actually goes up into the bowel wall. It's recognised to be an early feature of the bowel being abnormal itself and is recognised in necrotising enterocolitis or NEC. So pneumatosis is sometimes a sign of early necrotising enterocolitis.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes. So is that pneumatosis or might it be pneumatosis or what?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, it could be pneumatosis and it's reasonable on the basis of this imaging to put a provisional diagnosis of NEC.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Just remaining on the left-hand half of the image, we can see what appears to be a serpentine line running from the top down in an inverted L off to the left of the image. I'm sure everybody knows what that is, but could you just -- to remove all doubt, what is that, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think that's an ECG lead, actually.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that's external to the patient and has nothing to do with the bowel.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: No. Thank you. So moving across then, please, the image to where we see the three arrows centring in on what looks like a -- well, what we probably all now know is part of the bowel; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's right. It looks a bit like a sausage and the concern then -- if you think a sausage has two ends to it, the concern is that maybe the bowel has twisted on itself or is just a single loop that's become abnormal and distended, both of which are recognised to be abnormal in this context, so could be again features of necrotising enterocolitis.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's a phrase that you have used now more than once, I think, "could be features of necrotising enterocolitis".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: In determining that particular question, can you, as a radiologist, take the answer any further than in effect what you've just given us?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On a radiograph, you can't make a diagnosis of NEC unless the features are absolutely severe, which in this case are not, so these are sort of mild features. We also use the passage of time to diagnose NEC on X-ray, so subsequent radiographs are necessary to make a more convincing diagnosis. So on the basis of this alone, it would be reasonable to say that this could be early NEC and then you would need to correlate that with how [Baby Q] was behaving, temperature, how he was handling, et cetera.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes, which presumably you would defer to clinicians?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Just dealing with subsequent radiographs, as you've introduced them, we did earlier in our chronological list deal with the next two. They were taken the same day. The first was at 11.58, which puts us, in general terms, about 7 hours later, and the second was at 07.41, 3 days later. Did you see any similar suggestive images of NEC in either of those two radiographs?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the next radiograph in sequence, so the one at 11.58 on the same day, shows some of these similar features, but almost a little bit better. So they're resolving.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: But it's my understanding that it was on the basis of those two radiographs that he was transferred to Alder Hey again with a provisional or an understanding that he would need treatment for NEC.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So, so far as the image 6 or 7 hours later, that produced a better, a more encouraging picture than the one we see here; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that is the most severe, if you like, but even this in context is relatively mild.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you very much. Would you wait there, please? There may be some further questions for you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Can you see and hear me, Professor Arthurs?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I can now, thank you, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm just going to ask you about several of the radiographs you have just dealt with. The radiographs that were taken on 25 June, which we know is the day of the event the prosecution are looking at in particular, those were both principally chest radiographs, weren't they?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Right. I'm going to turn next then to the two radiographs we've just been dealing with, which are both on 26 June.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Your opinion is that the one which is timed 5.05 displays features that could be features of NEC; that's correct, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And the radiograph that's timed 11.58 shows, you say, similar features but they appear to be resolving?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Right. We've approached them by looking at 5.05 first and then 11.58.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: It's a matter that we can confirm, but I seem to recall from the evidence we've had, 5.05 has in fact been identified at 5.05 pm, not am.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Ah.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: If that's so, what we actually have with the two radiographs is a slight worsening in the condition of NEC, don't we, if it's that way round?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If it's that way round, yes. So if that's 5 pm, that's possible. But then we should look at the X-ray which is next in series, which is from Liverpool Alder Hey, which I think was taken at 20.22 in that series.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Can I ask why you think that that X-ray was done at 17.05 rather than 05.05? Because it's my understanding that the 05.05 timestamp is from the time that it was acquired in the hospital.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So I should say that was my understanding initially and that's how I dealt with it, but I seem to recall, and we can confirm, that we've had evidence, it may be from Dr Gibbs, but I would like it confirm this, that in fact that X-ray of 5.05 is in the afternoon and not the morning. But in any event, if that is right, that would show a worsening, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: We'll confirm that. I would like it checking if there's any uncertainty as to that. But in any event, both X-rays that we've looked at from that day display features of mild NEC, don't they?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And what you've identified is that to make a diagnosis beyond that, one needs to look at other features like how the baby -- how [Baby Q] was behaving on handling and any variation in temperature, things like that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, the clinical features need to match with the radiographic features, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you very much, Professor Arthurs.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Does your Lordship have any questions?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, the professor did say one then needs to look at the next radiograph at 20.22 if that's 17.05 hours.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just so we can clear it up.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Re-examination by MR JOHNSON
When you refer to 20.22, Professor Arthurs, which of the radiographs are you talking about?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: When you read through my report, that related to all of the X-rays that were done at the Countess of Chester Hospital,
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: which is correct in that series, but of course on the evening of 26 June I understand that [Baby Q] was transferred to Alder Hey.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: He was.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And there is an X-ray taken at 20.22 on 26 June, so immediately on admission, which shows -- of [Baby Q]'s abdomen, which shows there is gas in the distal bowel and effectively things are settling. So if we are to assume that the 5.05 radiograph was in fact 17.05 then my understanding is there's an X-ray at 11.58 that day that shows mild features, then an X-ray at 17.05 that day that shows slight worsening, which has then improved significantly by the time [Baby Q] arrives at Alder Hey at 20.22. So that's the reason just to mention that if there is significance in that interpretation.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Okay. So what you're saying is if the image that we have put up is 17.05 there is a further image that wasn't in the list that we dealt with earlier, taken 3 hours and about 10 or 15 minutes later, at Alder Hey, following the transfer, which shows a significant improvement?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Is that what you said?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So if [Baby Q] had NEC, it was very early, it was mild, and presumably resolved quite quickly.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes. That's very helpful, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm sorry, my Lord, I omitted to deal with that.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Does your Lordship have any further questions?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, Professor Arthurs. That concludes the evidence you're giving in this trial. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's the case, Professor Arthurs.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you very much for making yourself available, both in person on the occasions that you were here, and remotely. We're very grateful to you. That does complete your evidence. You won't be required again, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord, I'm very grateful.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: (The video link as terminated)
My Lord, may I recall, please, Sergeant Stonier, and we'll return to the interviews.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: DC DANIELLE STONIER (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR ASTBURY (continued)
Sergeant Stonier, we dealt with, on the last occasion, the first interview concerning [Baby A], which took place on 4 July 2018; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Just by way of reminder, if it's necessary, more than one baby was discussed on that date and the following day; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: But for presentation purposes we are dealing with or compartmentalising, if I can use that word, each baby in turn; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So rather than the next baby being discussed on 4 July, we're going to go to the next interview involving [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you. That should be behind divider 2, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Hopefully everyone has the frontispiece and a page [document redacted] on the top right-hand corner.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: These have been paginated in such a way that it's the baby but consecutive page numbers, so clearly the last interview was 23 pages but we've carried on the pagination individually for [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can see from the date, this is now 11 June 2019; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So the next occasion upon which the defendant was interviewed about [Baby A]; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: We heard some admissions on the last occasion to say that this was the next occasion upon which Lucy Letby was arrested by the police.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you. So if we can present them in the same fashion, please. I'll, as best I can, play the part of the police officers if you can give the answers that Ms Letby provided.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We heard last time about the caution, so there was a series of introductions and caution; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: People state their name. There's a wording to introduce the interview and then the suspect is reminded of the caution; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The reply from Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay, Lucy [says the officer], the first baby I'm going to talk to you about is [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He then continues: Do you agree, Lucy, that it was actually you who noticed the colour changing to [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I noticed the colour change, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Again, was it you, Lucy, who connected the fluids to [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, from my memory it -- it was Mel.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And then in summary, Ms Letby was asked whether she was standing or stood by [Baby A]'s incubator when he collapsed. She replied?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I was stood by the incubator carrying out my checks.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Were you stood by his incubator when his monitor sounded?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall exactly when his monitor sounded. If I was stood at his cot side then, yes, I would have heard the monitor. I agree I was stood at the incubator checking, carrying out my checks as I said before.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: But you don't remember the alarm sounding?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember specifically, no. It was a long time ago. I don't remember what monitor went off when.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. But do you remember you think that it was Nurse Taylor who connected the fluids then?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, but that is only from my memory.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: It's a long time ago.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yeah. No, I agree, as in the fluids. She did sit at the computer writing her notes while I was checking the fluids and everything else.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Is it at that point, Lucy, that you have caused harm to [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Is it at that point, Lucy, that you have murdered [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby was informed of the experts' view concerning air embolus, and she replied.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Well, I don't know how he would have received a bolus of air. From which line? Does it say which line?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: How would that be of significance, Lucy?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Um, because whoever did connect the fluids, either myself or Mel, they were connecting via a long line.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It'd be very hard to push air through a long line.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: See, you do know a little bit about it then, about air?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I know how we -- no, but I know how you flush fluids through a long line and that's a very -- it's a hard pressure to push through. I don't know how you'd push air through a long line.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So are you saying that this was an accident then, Lucy?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I am saying I don't know how that occurred but I did not do anything deliberately and, yes, they've quoted me being stood at the incubator, but that does that not mean I was doing anything untoward to [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was anyone else next to you by that incubator when the alarm sounded and stuff?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: From memory, Reg Harkness was in the room at all times.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: He was with [Baby B] and Caroline Bennion, another nurse, from memory, was in and out of the room.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So you remember that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: From memory, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: But you don't remember about the line? So you remember the line but you don't remember other issues about that particular collapse, do you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you deliberately inject air to [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I did not.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you see anyone else cause harm to [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you have any explanation, Lucy, for [Baby A]'s collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No. My concern at the time with [Baby A] was whether they -- there had potentially been an issue with either the fluids or the line because it was so quickly after the fluids had been connected that there was a problem.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Um, I know I had asked for all fluids to be kept, for the bag at the end to be checked. I don't know whether that was done or not. Do you know if --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Then you put:

blocks.text: Can you see that entry?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: Okay, "From all three drains".

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.

blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.

blocks.text: -- is something I hadn't seen a lot of on the unit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY
